title: Hosted API continuity protocol and tool binding - PRD ideation
summary: Draft proposal for a continuity protocol that makes streaming responses resumable and tool-calls transactional, plus SDK ergonomics patterns for surfacing partial structured outputs to clients. Focus is developer UX when networks fail, tool replay safety, and minimal server-side state while enabling predictable rollouts.
problem_statement: Customers build interactive features using streaming responses plus tool integrations. Current gaps: streaming sessions drop on flaky networks; partial tool side effects are hard to reason about; SDKs expose raw frames that are noisy; and rollbacks / retries lead to duplicate actions or poor UX. We need a lightweight protocol and SDK patterns that reduce engineering burden while preserving reliability and low latency.
proposal_overview: Introduce a continuity layer over the existing streaming API: session checkpoints, idempotent tool bindings, and typed partial-result envelopes. SDKs will wrap the wire protocol to provide convenience primitives: stream.resume(session_id, last_seq), tool.call.atomic(..., idempotency_key), and structuredPartial.applyCheckpoint(checkpoint). The server stores compact checkpoint digests (not full conversation state) to keep storage bounded.
success_metrics:
- Reduced median user-visible reconnection time from 7s to <1s for flaky mobile networks
- <1% customer-reported duplicated tool side effects after retries
- SDK adoption: 40% of new hosted-api integrations use continuity primitives within 3 months of GA
- Observability: 99% of resumed sessions reconcile without manual intervention
out_of_scope:
- Full conversational state storage for very long sessions (>24h)
- Complex distributed transactions spanning multiple external tools where external semantics cannot be made idempotent
- Replacing existing streaming wire formats entirely (we build compatibility layer)
user_stories:
- As a mobile app developer, I want streaming responses to continue after a short network drop so the chat UI doesn't show repeated loading states.
- As a platform integrator, I want tool calls to be safe to replay so webhook-triggered downstream systems are not duplicated.
- As an SDK user, I want simple APIs to get the latest structured partial results and an easy way to commit a final result.
- As an SRE, I want lightweight server checkpoints so storage and GC are predictable.
requirements:
Functional:
- R1: Server issues monotonic sequence numbers for frames and compact checkpoint tokens (checkpoint_id).
- R2: Clients can request resume by providing session_id + last_ack_seq or checkpoint_id.
- R3: Tool calls include an idempotency_key and explicit commit/abort semantics for at-most-once execution when supported by tool adapters.
- R4: Partial structured outputs are delivered in typed envelopes (status: partial|final|checkpoint) with machine-parseable schema hints.
Non-functional:
- R5: Checkpoint metadata per session must be <1KB and retained for configurable TTL.
- R6: Resume latency (server processing + first frame) must be <200ms for local-region resumes.
- R7: Backward compatibility: existing streaming clients should continue to receive frames unchanged if they ignore continuity headers.
api_surface_sketch:
- POST /v1/sessions -> creates session_id, returns initial checkpoint_id and TTL.
- POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/stream?resume=true with header X-Last-Ack: <seq> or X-Checkpoint: <id> -> server resumes stream from that point and issues missed frames if available.
- POST /v1/tools/call -> body includes tool, args, idempotency_key, optional commit_hint. Returns call_id and provisional result frames.
- POST /v1/tools/{call_id}/commit -> finalizes side effect; server returns final status.
Notes: headers are additive; we aim to keep wire backwards-compatible by adding X- continuity headers and preserving existing frame body format.
sdk_ergonomics:
Principles:
- Small mouthful APIs: start()/resume() and callTool() should cover 90% of flows.
- Higher-level primitives: StreamSession that exposes events: on('partial'), on('checkpoint'), on('toolResult'), on('final').
- Explicit but simple tool primitives: tool = client.tool('send-email'); tool.call(args, {idempotencyKey}) -> returns a Promise that resolves to provisional stream frames and exposes commit().
- Mobile-first: lightweight memory footprint, automatic reconnect with exponential backoff and transparent resume where possible.
- Observable-first: SDK emits telemetry hooks (checkpoint-created, resumed, tool-duplicated-detected) that can be lifted into Console dashboards.
Language specifics:
- Node/Python: Promise/async iterator patterns for incremental frames.
- Mobile (iOS/Android): delegate/callback patterns and a small state machine to surface resume states to the UI.
tool_calling_flow:
Sequence (typical):
1) Client constructs tool call with idempotency_key = uuid().
2) client POSTs tool.call; server responds with call_id and provisional frames (e.g., tool_event with status=started).
3) Server invokes adapter; adapter must honor idempotency_key if available.
4) Adapter returns provisional outputs which the server streams back.
5) Client may attach commit intent by calling tools/{call_id}/commit.
6a) On commit, server coordinates finalization and emits tool_event final.
6b) If commit never issued and adapter supports at-most-once, server garbage-collects provisional.
Safety notes: adapters must map idempotency_key to underlying provider semantics or provide compensating operations if true at-most-once cannot be guaranteed.
rollout_plan:
- Phase 0 (experiment): internal dogfood only, limited adapter set, opt-in flag for SDKs. Duration 4 weeks.
- Phase 1 (beta): invited customers, telemetry collection enabled, adapters for email/slack/webhook. Duration 8 weeks.
- Phase 2 (GA): default SDK behavior, docs, migration guide, console surface for checkpoint TTLs and resumed sessions.
Notes: provide migration scripts and deprecation timeline for clients that rely on exact frame counts.
risks_mitigation:
- Risk: Adapters cannot be made idempotent -> Mitigation: require adapters to declare semantics and offer a compensating-action pattern and advisory UI in console.
- Risk: Storage grows due to many checkpoints -> Mitigation: TTL-based GC, compact digests only, and optional external checkpoint store for large customers.
- Risk: Client-Server divergence on resume window -> Mitigation: server emits truncation notices and SDK surfaces a rehydrate flow that re-requests full state from a stable endpoint.
open_questions:
- What is the desired default checkpoint TTL and how configurable should it be per-customer?
- Should we permit multi-call transactions that atomically finalize multiple tool calls in one commit? (raises complexity)
- How to surface partial structured outputs in Console for non-technical users?
- Do we need a single standard schema registry or leave schema hints freeform?
notes:
Next steps: engineering spike to implement minimal checkpoint digest + replay window; solutions team to prototype adapter idempotency guidelines; SDK owners to produce a Node + mobile preview. Cross-ref with Console telemetry and product rollouts.
